species.title: Cameroon Hardwoods for Commercial Use
species.subtitle: We focus on commercially established, high-demand African hardwoods from Cameroon with proven international standards for marine, civil, joinery, and decorative applications.

items.name: Azobé
items.color: Dark red-brown to violet-brown with white mineral deposits
items.description: One of the heaviest and most durable commercial hardwoods in the world. Renowned for supreme resistance to marine borers, rot, and severe mechanical stress.

items.name: Tali
items.color: Yellow-orange to reddish-brown, darkening upon exposure
items.description: A very hard, dense African timber used increasingly across Europe and Asia as a premier alternative to Azobé for outdoor decking, civil structures, and heavy construction.
items.formsAvailable: Round logs, rough-sawn planks, and squared beams

items.name: Sapelli
items.color: Medium reddish-brown with luminous ribbon stripe figure
items.description: Prized globally as an exceptional African mahogany substitute. Features fine interlocked grain with distinctive ribbon figure, excellent workability, and rich warm luster.
items.formsAvailable: Kiln-dried & air-dried sawn timber, square logs

items.name: Padouk
items.color: Vivid coral orange-red when fresh, maturing to deep warm red
items.description: A spectacular African timber celebrated for its bold coral red coloration, extraordinary dimensional stability, and natural resistance to fungi and termites.
items.formsAvailable: Rough-sawn boards, dimensioned lumber, select logs

items.name: Ayous
items.description: Soft, lightweight, and uniform hardwood. Easy to machine, mould, and thermally modify for sauna interiors, framing, and light building elements.

items.name: Iroko
items.color: Golden yellow turning to rich bronze brown
items.description: Often referred to as African Teak for its remarkable weather resistance, stability, and oily grain that repels moisture in demanding outdoor environments.

faq.title: Straight Answers for Purchasing Managers & Importers
faq.subtitle: Clear, practical answers about our Cameroon hardwood species, volumes, dimensions, shipping routes, and export documentation.

questions.question: What timber species do you supply from Cameroon?
questions.answer: Our primary export focus is on Azobé (Lophira alata), Tali (Erythrophleum ivorense), Sapelli (Entandrophragma cylindricum), and Padouk (Pterocarpus soyauxii). In addition, we regularly supply Ayous (Obeche), Iroko, Bilinga, Sipo, and Doussié upon request. If you require another Cameroon species, contact our export desk and we will confirm current availability.

questions.question: Do you supply Azobé logs and heavy sawn beams?
questions.answer: Yes. Azobé can be supplied both as round sawlogs and as heavy rough-sawn structural beams (e.g. for marine piling, bridge construction, and harbor works). Because export rules and quota restrictions on specific log classes can vary, we confirm current log export authorization at the time of your inquiry.

questions.question: Do you supply sawn Sapelli in specific thicknesses?
questions.answer: Yes. Sawn Sapelli is one of our flagship products. We supply standard export thicknesses including 25mm, 32mm, 38mm, 50mm, 63mm, 75mm, and 100mm, in mixed or selected widths (100mm - 300mm+) and lengths (2.1m - 5.5m+). We provide both fresh-cut (green) and air-dried (AD) stock, as well as kiln-dried (KD 12-14%) upon contractual agreement.

questions.question: Can I purchase Tali in commercial bulk volumes?
questions.answer: Yes. Tali is widely requested by civil contractors and decking importers in Europe and Asia. We can quote multi-container monthly supply contracts as well as spot container loads, with volumes validated against our operational cutting schedule.

questions.question: Do you supply Padouk?
questions.answer: Yes, Padouk is quoted primarily as sawn timber and select decorative square logs. Sawn Padouk is prized for its intense red-coral hue and high dimensional stability. Please specify your target dimensions and any color grading criteria when submitting your inquiry.

questions.question: What is your Minimum Order Quantity (MOQ)?
questions.answer: Our standard minimum order is one 20ft container load (FCL), which typically holds between 18 and 23 m³ of dense hardwood sawn timber or equivalent log volume, depending on vessel weight limits and species density. For large projects, we handle multi-container and break-bulk charter shipments.

questions.question: How are timber volumes calculated and verified?
questions.answer: For sawn timber, volume is calculated as Net Metric Volume: Thickness (m) × Width (m) × Length (m) per individual piece, aggregated to three decimal places in cubic meters (m³). For round logs, volumes are measured according to standard forestry formula (Hoppus or Smalian based on agreed mid-point / end diameter and length under bark), listed piece-by-piece on the official packing list.

questions.question: Can I request photographs and inspection videos before shipment?
questions.answer: Absolutely. We encourage all buyers to review high-resolution photographs and video footage of representative stock during tallying, strapping, and container stuffing. You are also welcome to appoint an independent inspection agency (e.g. SGS, Bureau Veritas) or visit our yard in Cameroon prior to departure.

questions.question: Where does the timber ship from in Cameroon?
questions.answer: All international shipments originate in Cameroon and depart through either the Port of Douala or the Kribi Deep-Water Port, depending on vessel availability, shipping line routing, and cargo configuration.

questions.question: Do you export through Douala or Kribi?
questions.answer: We utilize both ports strategically. Douala handles steady containerized traffic to all major global transshipment hubs. Kribi's deep-water terminal accommodates large-draft vessels and direct container services, significantly reducing transit time for large cargo.

questions.question: Can Prime Wood Global arrange ocean freight?
questions.answer: Yes. We can quote on FOB (Douala or Kribi) or CFR / CIF to your discharge port of choice. We work directly with major ocean carriers (CMA CGM, Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd) to secure competitive maritime freight rates.

questions.question: How long does export processing and shipping take?
questions.answer: For existing yard stock, preparation, customs clearance, and phytosanitary processing take approximately 2 to 3 weeks before vessel loading. Ocean transit time depends on destination: typically 20-30 days to Mediterranean & North European ports, and 30-45 days to Asian ports.

questions.question: How is the timber packaged and secured for sea transit?
questions.answer: Sawn timber is neatly bundled by dimension and length, tightly secured with heavy-duty anti-rust steel straps, and fitted with timber dunnage for forklift handling. Bundles are marked with weather-resistant paint and tags identifying species, dimensions, and bundle numbers.

questions.question: What export documentation is provided with shipments?
questions.answer: Every export shipment includes a full documentary set: Commercial Invoice, Detailed Packing List & Tally Sheet, Official Phytosanitary Certificate from the Ministry of Agriculture, Certificate of Origin from the Cameroon Chamber of Commerce, and Ocean Bill of Lading (B/L). Sourcing and forestry compliance waybills are also supplied.

questions.question: What information should I include in my quotation request?
questions.answer: To receive a fast, accurate Proforma Invoice, please provide: (1) Timber species, (2) Product format (Logs, Rough-sawn, Dimensioned), (3) Dimensions (thickness × width × length), (4) Total volume (m³ or number of containers), (5) Moisture condition (Fresh, AD, or KD), (6) Destination country and discharge port, and (7) Preferred delivery incoterm (FOB or CIF).

questions.question: What payment terms are accepted for export orders?
questions.answer: We typically operate under international trade standards: Irrevocable Letter of Credit (L/C at sight) from a recognized prime international bank, or Telegraphic Transfer (T/T with deposit against order confirmation and balance against copy of shipping documents and Bill of Lading).
